items.title: Deep Learning From Scratch
items.why: The two architecture families CS231n and CS224d teach, as arithmetic a check can catch over A8's exact engine: the convolution and its transpose (the backward pass of a conv is the same op with the roles of input and filter swapped — the identity the mutation battery tests), pooling and its gradient as argmax routing, weight sharing as one parameter seen by every patch, stride and padding as index arithmetic with the boundary case named, a small net trained on a synthetic deterministic dataset (a fixed pattern the filters must become — the learned kernel compared against the planted one, not eyeballed); then the recurrent half: the RNN cell unrolled, BPTT as A8's reverse mode over the unroll (the vanishing gradient made a number: the norm of the gradient at step k versus k+1, exact), word vectors from counts and PMI before any gradient flows, seq2seq with the bottleneck that motivates attention, and the bridge stage: the same task solved by attention over A2's transformer, where the recurrence disappears and the sequential dependency is the thing being removed. No float anywhere; the dataset is data, not a download. Author deep-learning-from-scratch; A8 is the engine it trains through and A2 the transformer it ends at.

items.title: Continual Learning From Scratch
items.why: The forgetting experiment in exact rational arithmetic, as the capstone A8's engine exists to support: two linear tasks A and B on disjoint and overlapping input subspaces, exact SGD, forgetting measured as the exact prediction change |f_afterB(x_A) - f_beforeB(x_A)| — never a tolerance — and four families compared on identical tasks: naive joint fine-tune (forgetting > 0, reproducible, not asserted), progressive column addition (forgetting == Rational(0) by construction, capacity growing O(tasks)), parameter freeze (gradients exactly zero, but task B underfits on overlap — the capacity trade pinned), and deterministic replay (full replay converges to joint-training weights on A∪B exactly; partial replay upper-bounds forgetting recomputably). RIM and a program-tree module net extend the same engine: permutation equivariance and bit-identical composition, pinned. The four-family comparison table is the course.

items.title: CPU From Scratch

items.title: OS From Scratch
items.why: Built, and the salvage is part of it: `linux-from-scratch/` (the curriculum kept from the branch) is the prose, and ten graded stages are the course, on a provided machine (`machine.py`, `devices.py`, `userland.py`) whose promises break as soon as a program does something it should not. The thesis: an operating system is what you write after the hardware breaks your last promise. Join a boot map's regions and derive the frames a kernel may hand out; allocate frames from a bitmap that protects the frame its own bits live in and answers all or nothing; build page tables whose entries can never be read as frame numbers and check a permission bit on every walk, not just on the first; take a fault as a word a handler decides from rather than an exception; check a pointer before it is used and write the line that promises the act before the act; make a process a dict with a space, a ledger and a zombie at the end, and `fork` copy frames rather than table entries; pick by priority and age behind a quantum that rotates; put two CPUs on an interleaving where the critical section is a lock whose order is checked; format a real on-disk filesystem whose superblock is written last and mount only what a barrier made durable; and end on a userland whose kernel report is recomputed from its own log and cross-checked, key by key, against the machine's records.

items.title: Runtime From Scratch
items.why: A language runtime makes two promises — the program runs, and memory stops being your problem — and a provided bytecode, assembler and heap are where you keep both. The acceptance is a program's own output plus its collection counts, and the one invariant a collector may never break: nothing reachable is ever collected, and no uncollected frame is ever read. items.title: Coreutils From Scratch
items.why: The tools the terminal is made of, each one a byte-oriented contract: grep is a matcher whose anchors, classes and -v inversion are decisions, not flags; tail is circulation over a fixed buffer for -n and a backward scan for -c, and its -f is a polling loop the harness drives tick by tick; sort's merge and key spec; wc's count that must be wrong the same way GNU is wrong when the last line lacks its newline; and an editor that is a gap buffer, a screen model of rows and columns over those bytes, and the redraw that shows exactly the cursor's truth. Each command is judged byte-for-byte against the real one on provided corpora, the editor against scripted keystrokes and the frame it must have drawn. items.why: The big one, and the only project in this repository where the acceptance is real hardware obeying you: a bootable x86-64 kernel in C and a userland on top, built end to end — GRUB or your own bootloader handing control at the magic number, the GDT and IDT you write by hand, the PIT and the APIC and the timer that makes time exist, physical and virtual memory with the page tables QEMU's `info page-tables` can show you, interrupts where a keypress becomes a scan code becomes a character on your own screen, the scheduler you proved as data in G4 now context-switching for real, the syscall entry with its privilege ring crossing and the user pointer you must validate twice, drivers written against the device rather than a model: the PS/2 controller's ports and its second-byte wait, the ATA identify and the read sector that polls its status register, PCI enumeration walking the config space bus by bus, and the e1000 or virtio NIC whose ring you fill and whose interrupt you share; a ramdisk and then a real filesystem on a disk image, an ELF loader so a program you compiled with G5 runs as a process with its own address space, fork and exec and wait as real code, and the shell from G7 speaking to your kernel instead of another's. The graded path is the x86-64 stages; the arm64 port is the second half. Author custom-os-from-scratch in C; G4's simulator is the model, G5 the toolchain, linux-from-scratch/ the prose.

items.title: Advanced Algorithms & Data Structures
items.why: La Rocca's book mechanised, one stage per chapter, every structure judged against a work counter and a reference the way B2 judges HNSW against brute force: priority queues and d-way heaps measured on Dijkstra (ch. 2), treaps where the rotation is right because the expected height the profiler prints agrees with the theory (ch. 3), Bloom filters whose false-positive rate is measured, not assumed, against the exact set (ch. 4), disjoint sets by path compression and union by rank counted in finds (ch. 5), tries and T9 and autocomplete with the compressed variant (ch. 6), LRU and LFU caches with the hit rate the workload produces (ch. 7), k-d trees whose nearest neighbour is checked against the linear scan it must beat (ch. 8–9), SS-trees and approximate search with the recall the book's own image retrieval asks for (ch. 10–11), DBSCAN and OPTICS clustering on the points the reference clusters identically (ch. 12–13), graphs from BFS and connected components to Dijkstra and minimum spanning trees (ch. 14), graph embeddings, planarity and the force-directed drawing whose crossings the checker counts (ch. 15), then gradient descent (ch. 16) and simulated annealing (ch. 17) as optimisation on those graphs, and the genetic algorithm that closes the book on TSP, its tours compared against the branch-and-bound answer on the small instances (ch. 18). Author advanced-dsa-from-scratch in pure Python with no float where a counter suffices — nothing must come first; the book is the reading, the checker the grade.

items.title: SQLite From Scratch
items.why: The database embebida, from the recovered codecrafters corpus (codecrafters-reference/sqlite/, nine stages with the tester's own commands): a real single-file database that `sqlite3` itself opens. Parse the database header and walk the schema table whose rows are the other tables; decode a table B-tree page by page — cell pointer array, varints, overflow pages — until `SELECT` over your file returns the rows sqlite3 returns; build the record format serial types and the freelist; then the write half: the WAL, the commit that is not acknowledged before the WAL says so, and the crash that loses nothing. The judge is sqlite3 itself reading what you wrote and the row counts matching on the files both wrote. H5 is the query engine; this is the storage layer it runs on, done for real. Author sqlite-from-scratch.

items.title: Regex From Scratch
items.why: The one language every tool in phase G already assumes, taught by building the engine twice: Thompson's construction first — parse with the shunting yard, compile to an NFA whose states are epsilon-closures, simulate in linear time — then the backtracking engine, whose catastrophic cases (`(a+)+$`) the work counter exposes by the seconds it burns where the NFA spent microseconds. Character classes, anchors, quantifiers greedy and lazy, groups and backreferences the NFA refuses (and why PCRE pays for them), then the integration that gives the course its teeth: grep (G9) re-derives its -E from this engine, tail -f's scrollback filter and G7's shell globs borrow the same compile step, and the judge is the match sets agreeing with Python's `re` on a corpus built to distinguish the two engines. Author regex-from-scratch; nothing must come first.

items.title: Reverse Engineering
items.why: The discipline of reading a program you do not have the source for, taught on binaries you can verify: the ELF and PE formats as data — headers, sections, symbols, relocations — parsed until `readelf` and yours agree; x86-64 disassembly with the length-decoding problem that makes it not just a table (prefixes, ModRM, the cases where data is code and back); the calling conventions and the stack frame reconstructed from prologues; control-flow recovery — the CFG from a linear sweep and the recursive descent and where they disagree; the decompilation lift to a C-like IR and what it always gets wrong; then the dynamic half: the ptrace attach, breakpoints, the memory dump, the syscall trace that tells you what the binary does when the static reading lies; strings, imports and the entropy profile that finds the packed sections; and the capstone, a crackme and a stripped binary from the provided estate, where the licence check must be found, understood and described — the judge being the write-up whose every claim (function boundaries, the key derivation, the anti-debug trick) is checked against ground truth the estate carries. Built with the tools, not around them: objdump, gdb, radare2 are the reference outputs your own parser and lifter are checked against. Author reverse-engineering-from-scratch; G3 built the CPU, G5 built the compiler — this reads what they emit, without the source.

Author agent-optimization-from-scratch; C2 is the agent the pipeline wraps, C1 the harness the metric is held out through, and A8 the engine the acceptance rule runs on.

items.title: Hierarchical Sequences
items.why: Token resolution as the architecture's own decision, priced and probed in exact arithmetic: the pooling cost ledger (pool_len's ragged tail, quadratic attention work down to 1/16 and 15/16 at k=4), the S_k permutation invariance of mean-pooling and the witness that is provably unrecoverable from a pooled value, Hourglass's shift-by-(k-1) causality law that makes a funnel autoregressive, BLT's entropy-threshold patching and H-Net's learned boundary against the fixed strip, and the BPE counterexample. The invariant, not the trained funnel — the claims of the four papers stay cited reading.

items.title: Recursive Depth (HRM/TRM)
items.why: The two-timescale skeleton and the dispute, both checkable: a coupled recurrence as exact fixed-point iteration on a grid puzzle, halting iff the next state is byte-identical (Kleene–Tarski on a monotone finite lattice), verified by an independent constraint check — and then the ARC-AGI dispute as graded stages: the single-rate ablation that barely moves the score, the identity-conditioning collapse, and the TRM paper's own fixed-point violation counted exactly. What the skeleton does and does not claim.

items.title: Library Learning (DreamCoder)
items.why: The sleep phase as arithmetic: MDL-gated refactoring over a corpus of exact symbolic programs — a generalized subexpression promoted iff its version-space intersection is non-empty, its utility ledger is positive, and promotion is monotone (solved tasks stay solved, description length strictly decreases); wake as bottom-up enumeration over a rational-expression DSL, dream as deterministic recombination, and Voyager's gate — only verifier-accepted programs enter the library — which is this repo's own audit rule reused.

items.title: Causal Invariance (ICP)
items.why: The whole method, exact: environments as integer tuples, per-environment regression over Fractions, the exact conditional permutation p-value over all C(n+m,n) label assignments of pooled residuals, accept S iff p > alpha, the answer the intersection of accepted S — plus the over-acceptance case two environments cannot resolve, the mechanism-shift table, and the null case. items.title: Redis From Scratch
items.why: The in-memory store whose protocol is the lesson: RESP byte by byte, the command table a dict of (arity, handler) that refuses an arity it does not name, the store as a dict with per-key expiry where a lazy pass on read and an active cycle on the clock both evict, and an RDB the course parses byte by byte before it writes one. Then the hard half: AOF as a journal whose every line is a prediction until fsync makes it a fact (J3's discipline, at the file's mercy), and leader-follower replication where the follower's acknowledgement is state the leader keeps and the offset is the number both sides agree on. Accepted on a session the harness replays byte for byte, with the world's own RESP reader as the referee. Source: the 124-stage CodeCrafters corpus in `codecrafters-reference/redis/`.

items.title: Kafka From Scratch
items.why: The log as the product: the fetch/produce request envelopes of the real protocol, a partition as an append-only log with an offset cursor per consumer group, and the delivery contract decided, not assumed — at-least-once through redelivery deadline and dedup by id, at-most-once by committing the cursor before the work, exactly-once by idempotent producer sequence numbers. L2 is the framing half of a wire and J1 is the queue whose delivery semantics this course makes the broker's own decision. Source: the 25-stage CodeCrafters corpus in `codecrafters-reference/kafka/`.

items.title: Docker From Scratch
items.why: A container is isolation you can name: a chroot whose root is an overlay of layers, a PID and network and mount namespace the process is born into, cgroups that charge CPU and memory all or nothing, and capabilities that decide what the process may still do — the image as a stack of layers addressed by digest, `pull` resolving a manifest, `run` building the mount table before the exec, and a health check the container answers about itself. The namespaces are G4's process table made real and the capability gate is J4's, applied to a process that actually runs. Source: the 6-stage CodeCrafters corpus in `codecrafters-reference/docker/`, mocker and bocker in `tutorials-reference/`.

items.title: Emulator From Scratch

G3 is the datapath habit; here the *programs* are provided (the ROMs) and their accepted behaviour is the answer key. Source: the CHIP-8 tutorials in `tutorials-reference/chip8-python/` and the LC-3 VM.

items.title: RL Control From Scratch
items.why: Control as arithmetic over a value function: a world that is a Markov chain you can step (a gridworld, a gambler, a random walk — deterministic, seeded, its optimal policy computable by hand), then the estimation of that policy from experience alone — dynamic programming first, because the answer key is checkable, then Monte-Carlo returns and their first-visit variance, TD(0) and the bootstrapping that makes it biased, SARSA against Q-learning and what off-policy costs, a function approximator over A8's exact autograd engine for the state the table cannot hold, and a report whose every number (returns, regret, the policy's own actions) the world can recompute. Source: RL-from-zero and dennybritz's notebooks, in `tutorials-reference/`.

items.title: Git From Scratch
items.why: The one artefact in this repository that another program validates: a `.git` directory that real `git` reads. Blobs addressed by their own digest, trees whose entries are sorted and whose modes are exact, a commit with an author, a message and a parent, refs and a HEAD that can be detached; then the half that makes it a tool — an index that stages, a diff that names a hunk, a merge that finds the base and marks a conflict instead of guessing, and a packfile whose objects are delta-compressed and whose index lets a random read land without walking the file. A byte-oriented filesystem and a git-compatible reader are provided, and where `git` is on PATH the tester runs it: `git fsck` and `git log` have to accept your objects. items.title: Distressed Debt Investing
items.why: The same default seen from the buy side, where it is an opportunity with a price: the capital structure as a waterfall of claims over M1's borrower — who is owed what, secured ahead of whom — the distressed bond and loan bought below par, and the question every price asks: recovery, reorganisation, or the debtor's death; the distressed exchange and the maturity extension as the negotiated outcomes, the restructuring waterfall applied to the absolute-priority rule and the violations that settle it in practice, the claim the fund bought valued three ways — the expected recovery from M3's actual cash flows, the Merton distance-to-default on the borrower's own assets, and the comparables — and where the three disagree is the trade; the entry price implied return and the IRR in basis points that survives the timing of the recovery, the hold decision against the carry, and the report the fund writes: why this claim, at this price, with what recovery and by when — checked against what actually happened to the borrower. Author distressed-debt-from-scratch over M1's book and M3's collections log; the bank's provisioning and the fund's thesis are two readings of one default.

items.title: LBO Model From Scratch
items.why: The leveraged buyout as arithmetic that either holds or does not, built over M1's amortisation machinery and M3's workout realism: the target as facts — EBITDA, capex, working capital, the cap table — on a provided estate whose five-year path is the ground truth; the sources and uses that balance to the cent, entry multiple and financing structure as the two decisions that set everything; the debt schedule as a waterfall of tranches with covenants the model cannot quietly violate — revolver drawn when cash falls short, mandatory prepayment from excess cash, the incurrence test checked every period; the operating build from revenue to EBITDA to free cash flow with integer arithmetic and the day-count from M1; exit on the multiple the estate actually realises, and the returns decomposition the sponsor's own memo contains: how much of the IRR is leverage, how much is EBITDA growth, how much is multiple expansion — each named, each checked against the estate. Sensitivity as the model's honesty: the grid over entry price, exit multiple and leverage where the downside case breaches the covenant and the checker demands the breach be visible, not amortised away. Author lbo-model-from-scratch; M5 values the claim on the way down, M6 buys the whole company on the way in — two prices, one discipline: the cash flows decide.

items.title: Privacy Gateway & Delegated Access
items.why: The gateway between the agent and the world, as data a check can read back: sensitive values tokenized before the context window and restored after (deterministic masking, UUID swapping, the pre-flight/post-flight proxy), per-agent least privilege with scoped tool sets, then the identity half — machine identities rather than user sessions: an OAuth2 grant flow where the agent holds a heavily scoped, time-limited token minted for one action class instead of the user's credentials, the human-in-the-loop approval gate that stops the flow at a person and journals the decision, and the agent-to-agent trust boundary where one agent's output becomes another's input and the sanitizer must run on the seam. The audit line answers 'what did it touch'. Author agent-privacy-from-scratch; J4 is the sandbox half, D1 the protocol the tools speak, N4 the crypto the tokens and MACs stand on.

items.title: Grammar-Constrained Decoding
items.why: Enforcement at the token level, where 'please don't' cannot reach: a context-free grammar compiled to a mask such that every decode step scores only the tokens the grammar accepts — the mask as an intersection of the FSM state with the vocabulary, computed per step and provably complete (no valid continuation is ever masked), the JSON-schema subset compiled to that grammar, regex constraints as the DFA special case, the token-boundary problem where one token straddles two grammar states and the correct answer is to mask both halves or split the token, and the guarantees measured rather than asserted: schema-validity of a thousand constrained generations is exactly 1, the unconstrained baseline's is the number that makes the constraint worth its latency cost. Over A2's sampling loop and I3's continuous batching, where the mask cost per step is the budget line. Author grammar-decoding-from-scratch; H2 is the serving stack the sampler lives in.

items.title: Blockchain From Scratch
items.why: A ledger is a hash chain plus a rule for who appends: the block header and the digest that seals it, Merkle trees and the inclusion proof that is the point of them, addresses and signatures over a provided keypair scheme, the UTXO set and the spend that must name what it consumes, the mempool and the double-spend the ordering kills, proof-of-work's target and difficulty adjustment as the two constants that make a chain honest about time, then proof-of-stake's slots and attestations on the same world, fork choice as a rule recomputable from any node's own view, and a network of simulated peers whose clocks and drops the harness drives — accepted when every node converges on the same chain and a planted fork with less honest weight loses. Author blockchain-from-scratch; H6 is the agreement half taken seriously, N1 the ledger half.

stages.title: The header and the digest that seals it
stages.action: Write ``HEADER_KEYS``, ``spawn``, ``seal``, and ``link`` in stage_01.py.
stages.predict: What the all-zeros genesis invariant does to block 0, and how a single wrong character in prev_hash breaks the chain.

stages.title: Merkle trees and the inclusion proof
stages.action: Write ``MERKLE_KEYS``, ``leaves``, ``root``, ``proof``, and ``confirm`` in stage_02.py.
stages.predict: Why an odd number of transactions changes the root compared to padding with zeros, and how a single-bit change is caught in the proof.

stages.title: Addresses and the signature that binds
stages.action: Write ``ADDR_KEYS``, ``SIGN_KEYS``, ``_wallet``, ``witness``, and ``verify_input`` in stage_03.py.
stages.predict: Why a signature made for one transaction is refused on another, and what the public key in the challenge prevents.

stages.title: The UTXO set and the spend that names what it consumes

items.title: Smart Contracts & dApp
items.why: A contract is a program the ledger agrees to run exactly once, priced by the work it does: the account model over N1's UTXO world, the bytecode VM — stack, memory, storage whose every cold slot is charged — and the gas schedule that makes the meter real; a compiler from a toy contract language to that bytecode with the ABI that lets a caller encode a call; the escrow, the token and the voting contracts written in it, each with the reentrancy or overflow bug the tester plants and the checker asks your guard about; then the dApp on top: a local node your client talks to, transactions signed, sent and receipted, events indexed by your own scanner, and the front-end state machine that reads the chain and never trusts it. Author dapp-from-scratch; N1 is the machine it runs on.

items.title: MuJoCo-Style Physics Engine
items.why: A physics engine is a constraint solver wearing a scene graph: rigid bodies with mass and inertia tensors, contact detection as narrowphase over provided shapes, the contact Jacobian and the LCP that a projected solver iterates to rest, the warm start that makes it stable, the integrator's order and its energy drift, actuators and PD control, then a MuJoCo-shaped MJCF subset parsed into that world — and the proof of the whole thing: the gradients. MuJoCo exists because differentiable simulation trains controllers; A8's exact reverse mode over the solver's unrolled steps is the capstone, checked against the finite-difference oracle at every parameter. Author physics-engine-from-scratch; A8 is the engine that makes the last stage possible.

items.title: Cryptography From Scratch
items.why: The number theory applied until it encrypts something, in the repo's exact-arithmetic discipline (integers and polynomial coefficients only, no float): modular arithmetic and the extended Euclid that inverts in it, primes as generated facts (trial division first, then the Miller-Rabin witness that makes a composite name itself), the Chinese Remainder Theorem as a speedup you can measure, RSA from n = pq through the correctness proof (m^(ed) = m mod n, derived not asserted) to the textbook-RSA-is-broken list — deterministic padding or refusal, with the provided RNG the only seeded source — Diffie-Hellman over a safe prime and the discrete-log table that shows why small p is a toy, then GF(2^8) as a quotient ring: multiplication by the polynomial x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x + 1, the AES S-box derived from the multiplicative inverse rather than tabulated, and the MixColumns matrix applied by hand. The provided keypair scheme and N1's signatures are the consumers; the ungraded cryptographic-library/ C port is the second language this spec translates to. Author cryptography-from-scratch; G5 is the compiler that could port it to C byte for byte.

items.title: QR Codes & Error Correction
items.why: Coding theory with a camera as the judge, over GF(2^8) arithmetic a check can catch: the finite field built from the QR primitive polynomial 0x11d and carried as log/antilog tables, Reed-Solomon as polynomial evaluation — the message is a polynomial, the codeword is its values, the parity is the remainder of division by the generator — then the syndrome decoder that turns corrupted bytes back into a locator polynomial, Berlekamp-Massey as exact integer work, and the erasure case QR actually uses (the reader knows which modules are unreadable, and that halves the correction budget honestly). On top of the math, the spec: mode segments and byte capacity by version, the Reed-Solomon block interleaving that spreads a smudge across blocks, the eight masks scored by the penalty rules and the best mask named by the score, format and version information protected by their own BCH codes, and the encoder whose output a real phone decodes — the one judge outside the repo that is allowed. Author qr-codes-from-scratch.

items.title: Graphics From Scratch
items.why: The rasterization pipeline with the pixel as the judge, in the repo's exact-arithmetic discipline: a frame is a lattice of integer pixels whose colours are exact mixtures, and every stage's check compares the frame pixel-for-pixel — 'this pixel is exactly red' beats any image-diff tolerance. The ladder: lines by Bresenham's integer error accumulation, polygons filled by integer edge functions (the winding sign that is the whole barycentric idea), triangles rasterized by exact barycentric coordinates with tie-breaking the top-left rule names, a z-buffer whose depth interpolation is exact so a tie is decidable by ==, vertex transforms as exact matrix-vector products (translate, scale, rotate by integer cosine), viewport mapping with the off-by-one the half-pixel centres carry, clipping by exact comparisons against the frame's bounds, a painter-vs-z-buffer race settled by depth order, texture sampling on a lattice with nearest lookup and the seam the wrap rule chooses, and the capstone options the GPU analogy completes: a tiny ray tracer whose ray-sphere intersection is an exact quadratic at lattice distances, or a matrix-stack scene graph walking transforms the way G1's vGPU executes them. Author rasterizer-from-scratch; N3's physics supplies the geometry the camera watches.
